title: When Seeing Is Not Enough: Benchmarking Interactive Visual Grounding in LVLMs
abstract: arXiv:2608.23978v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Visual grounding is typically evaluated as a one-shot mapping from an informative referring expression to a visual target. This formulation misses a central property of real-world reference: target information is often incomplete, ambiguous, and established through interaction. We introduce a controlled evaluation framework for interactive visual grounding in large vision-language models (LVLMs), varying how much target information is provided upfront and how much must be acquired through dialogue. Across four human-grounded visual contexts and four interaction protocols, current LVLMs perform significantly below task-level human baselines. Interaction can help when follow-up questions refine or repair an initial target description. Performance is lowest when no initial description is provided and target information must be acquired through questions, indicating that proactive question-driven grounding remains difficult. translated_title: 当看见不够时：在LVLMs中基准测试交互式视觉定位
translated_abstract: 视觉定位通常被评估为从信息丰富的指代表达式到视觉目标的一次性映射。这种表述忽略了现实世界参考的一个核心属性：目标信息往往不完整、模糊，并通过交互建立。我们引入了一个受控评估框架，用于大型视觉语言模型（LVLMs）中的交互式视觉定位，变化了预先提供多少目标信息以及需要通过对话获取多少信息。在四种人类基础的视觉情境和四种交互协议下，当前LVLMs的性能显著低于任务级人类基线。当后续问题细化或修正初始目标描述时，交互可能有所帮助。当没有提供初始描述且必须通过问题获取目标信息时，性能最低，表明主动的问题驱动的定位仍然困难。LVLMs也面临挑战，p
tldr: 本文提出了一种交互式视觉定位基准测试框架，发现LVLMs在信息不完整或需通过对话获取目标时性能显著低于人类，凸显了主动提问式定位的困难。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces a benchmark for interactive visual grounding, showing that LVLMs perform significantly below human baselines when target information is incomplete or must be acquired through dialogue, highlighting the difficulty of proactive question-driven grounding.
